name: mrboom
why: Eight-player terminal Bomberman clone; fun and obscure, though a fairly standard game idea.

brief.what_it_is: Mr.Boom is a Bomberman clone, with up to eight players at the same time. The homepage says it is now available for RetroArch/Libretro and SDL2, with Windows binaries and a macOS install via Homebrew. The original was an MS-DOS game that used IPX networking for multiplayer, and the page offers a v3.0 MS-DOS download. The homepage does not describe inputs or outputs beyond the game itself. The scout note calls it a terminal game, but the homepage never says that, and it mentions SDL2 and RetroArch instead.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no stated purpose. It is a fan-style page for the game, mostly listing the author's favourite links and tools, with the tagline "welcome to the jungle...".

commands_seen.context: Homebrew install line for the macOS (OSX) version, listed on the homepage.

brief.install_notes: The homepage lists RetroArch/Libretro and SDL2 builds, Windows binaries, and the MS-DOS v3.0 download. Packages are listed on repology.org. The original DOS version needed IPX networking, and the page mentions DOS or Windows 95/98 for it. Joypad use on the DOS version relied on third-party adapters such as joyemu, keyemu, sneskey and directpad pro. I did not find first-run or configuration steps on the homepage.
brief.standout: It keeps an old-web personality: a 1990s-era fan page with a list of favourite links, MP3 pages and demoscene references. It also has an eight-player mode, which is unusual for a Bomberman clone.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage lists current ports (RetroArch/Libretro, SDL2, brew and repology packaging), which suggests some upkeep. The page itself looks old, has no date, and I found no release date or last commit. I did not reach the GitHub project page because its URL did not come through.
brief.caveats: The homepage is mostly a fan page and gives little technical detail. The GitHub project link is not resolved in my fetch, so I could not check the README, license, or recent activity. The scout note's 'terminal' description is not supported by the homepage. The DOS-era multiplayer depended on IPX and old hardware.
quotes: up to 8 players at the same time !!!
Even Microsoft can't save the world from MrBoomification
fetch_log: https://mrboom.mumblecore.org/ - loaded. Homepage content only; the GitHub project link text appeared but its URL was not in the returned text, so I did not follow it.
